briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have seen a significant escalation in military activities across the Middle East, most critically marked by direct Iranian ballistic missile strikes against US forces in Jordan and joint US-Saudi airstrikes against Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, resulting in at least 20 casualties. Simultaneously, the Strait of Hormuz remains a central flashpoint, with Iran asserting increased control and threatening international shipping, while Hezbollah's first ceasefire violation in southern Lebanon signals a deteriorating stability on Israel's northern border.

IRAN
Iranian military operations included the IRGC Aerospace Force targeting US military air base and central command headquarters in Jordan with multiple ballistic missiles early on July 29, which CENTCOM reported were all successfully intercepted without damage or casualties. Jordan's authorities also reported intercepting five missiles from Iran. Additionally, the IRGC claimed to have attacked three tankers attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz. Iran also confirmed the martyrdom of Brigadier General Majid Kazemi, an Su-24 pilot involved in a March 2026 strike on Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that an earlier attack on an Iranian cargo ship by Ukraine was deemed unintentional by Kyiv, though Iran seeks compensation and does not desire escalation.

In response to alleged drone attacks, US and Saudi forces conducted joint airstrikes against pro-Iranian militia targets in eastern Iraq, which Iranian and Iraqi sources reported resulted in at least 20 deaths and 32 injuries among the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF). The Iranian news agency Fars also reported an "enemy missile" striking an uninhabited area in West Azerbaijan, north-west Iran. Internally, Iran's intelligence forces announced the destruction of four terror cells and the arrest of 15 terrorists in the southeast.

Economically, global oil prices have reportedly surged by 7% to over $90 a barrel following the heightened tensions and threats from the US. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Garibabadi declared that the Strait of Hormuz would "never return to its pre-war state," rejecting an Omani proposal for shared control and threatening any European warship approaching the strait as a "legitimate target." Reuters also reported that Iran expects to receive 300 to 400 Chinese shoulder-fired air-defense missiles (QW-12 and FN-16) valued at $60-70 million within weeks to bolster its short-range air defense capabilities.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included the reopening of the 193rd Squadron of naval helicopters at Palmachim Airbase, enhancing maritime operational response. In Gaza, the IDF struck and destroyed several Hamas weapon depots, including one located inside a mosque in the northern Strip, citing the use of civilian infrastructure for terror. The IDF also killed Muhammad Khalil Muhammad Aslam, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander, in Khan Younis, citing his role in abducting Israeli civilians on October 7, 2023, and his recent advancement of attacks. In southern Lebanon, IDF forces demolished a 55-meter Hezbollah underground command center found beneath a construction material factory in Haddatha and located dozens of weapons. Troops also fired upon a suspect in Ras al-Bayada who approached them "in a manner that posed a threat."

No Israeli casualties were reported in a Hezbollah drone attack on an IDF engineering vehicle in southern Lebanon. On the home front, a false alarm for rocket fire was activated in Nahal Oz, and an interceptor missile was mistakenly launched over Metula towards Israeli artillery fire in southern Lebanon, with no resulting injuries or damage.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu held meetings with US Vice President J.D. Vance and President Donald Trump in Washington, with Netanyahu describing the discussion as "one of his best" and focusing on preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. An Israeli official indicated Trump did not demand an Israeli withdrawal from any front. The Israeli cabinet approved an initial proposal for Ugandan forces to join an International Stabilization Force in Gaza. Justice Minister Ben Gvir called for the death penalty for rapists, describing some incidents as having "nationalistic characteristics." Three Israeli settlement activists from the "Bashan Pioneers" group illegally crossed into Syria from the Mount Hermon area and were apprehended by IDF troops. A member of a civilian defense squad was arrested in connection with a settler rampage in Huwara in June. An Israeli civilian who served in a classified military unit was charged with spying for Iran.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, an Israeli strike in Khan Younis killed Muhammad Khalil Muhammad Aslam, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad platoon commander responsible for abducting Israeli civilians during the October 7, 2023, attack. The IDF also targeted and destroyed several Hamas weapon depots in central and northern Gaza, including one located within a mosque, emphasizing the terror organizations' use of civilian infrastructure. Efforts are underway to form an International Stabilization Force for Gaza, with Uganda reportedly approving an initial proposal to contribute troops.

In the West Bank, a UN official expressed alarm over the "rapidly deteriorating" situation and the escalation of settler attacks against Palestinians. An Israeli civilian, a member of a civil defense squad, was arrested for his involvement in a settler rampage in Huwara in June.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched an explosive drone attack against an IDF engineering vehicle (D9) in the Ali Taher Ridge area of southern Lebanon overnight, marking the first violation of the ceasefire agreement established in late June. No injuries were reported. The IDF condemned the attack as a "blatant violation" and stated it is deliberating a response. Israeli forces operating in the south Lebanon buffer zone also uncovered and destroyed a 55-meter Hezbollah underground command center, with three rooms, located beneath a construction material factory in the village of Haddatha, approximately 300 meters from a UNIFIL building. Dozens of weapons, including assault rifles, RPGs, and explosive devices, were found nearby. IDF artillery bombarded areas in Nabatieh. An Israeli interceptor missile was mistakenly launched at Israeli artillery fire towards Lebanon, with no reported damage or injuries.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iraq has become a major flashpoint following joint airstrikes by the US and Saudi Arabia targeting pro-Iranian militia positions in eastern Iraq. The strikes, which US CENTCOM stated were in response to over 30 drone attacks on US forces and Saudi oil infrastructure in the past 72 hours, reportedly killed at least 20 and injured 32 members of the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), according to Iranian and Iraqi sources. Targets included locations in Nineveh, Diyala, Kirkuk, Karbala, Wasit, and Basra.

In a direct response, Iran's IRGC Aerospace Force claimed to have launched ballistic missiles targeting US military air base and central command headquarters in Jordan, though CENTCOM reported all missiles were successfully intercepted.

The Iraqi government, including its President, former Prime Minister Al-Sudani, and influential religious and political figures like Muqtada al-Sadr, strongly condemned the US-Saudi strikes as a "blatant violation of Iraqi sovereignty" and called for the expulsion of US forces and review of ties with Saudi Arabia. Muqtada al-Sadr also called on Iran's IRGC to refrain from targeting Iraqi soil. The planned visit of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi to Saudi Arabia was subsequently cancelled.

Three Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed into Syria from the Mount Hermon area and were returned by the IDF.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia actively participated in joint airstrikes with the US against pro-Iranian militias in eastern Iraq. The Saudi Ministry of Defense also reported intercepting several drones launched from Iraq targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province, reserving the right to respond. Due to the US-Saudi strikes in Iraq, the planned meeting between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was cancelled.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical area of tension. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister explicitly stated that the strait would not revert to its pre-war status, rejected an Omani proposal for a 50/50 control split, and warned that any European warship approaching the strait would be a "legitimate target." An Iranian military commander reiterated that no movement would occur in the Strait of Hormuz without Iran's authorization. Iran also claimed to have struck three tankers attempting to cross the strait. Separately, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis are reportedly considering implementing transit fees for commercial vessels in the Red Sea, following their declaration of a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia.

The Algerian President sharply criticized an unnamed "regional micro-state," widely understood as the UAE, for its destabilizing activities across the Arab world and the Sahel region.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Saudi Joint Airstrikes in Iraq:** Joint US and Saudi air forces conducted strikes on July 28 against over 30 Iran-backed militia targets, including logistics and weapon depots, across eastern Iraq (Nineveh, Diyala, Kirkuk, Karbala, Wasit, Basra), reporting at least 20 killed and 32 injured.
2.  **Iranian Ballistic Missile Strikes on Jordan:** On July 29, Iran's IRGC Aerospace Force launched ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan; CENTCOM confirmed all missiles were intercepted with no casualties or damage.
3.  **Hezbollah Ceasefire Violation in Lebanon:** On July 29, a Hezbollah explosive drone struck an IDF engineering vehicle (D9) in the Ali Taher Ridge area of southern Lebanon, marking the first violation of the ceasefire agreement, with no reported injuries.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Control Asserted by Iran:** Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister announced Iran's intention to maintain increased control over the Strait of Hormuz, rejected Oman's mediation proposal, and threatened any European warships near the strait. Iran also claimed to have attacked three tankers.
5.  **US Senate Advances Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill:** The US Senate approved a bill (86-12) to extend the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to 2031 and impose sanctions on Russia.
6.  **Iran Acquiring Chinese Air Defense Missiles:** Reuters reported that Iran expects to receive 300-400 Chinese shoulder-fired air-defense missiles worth $60-70 million within weeks.
7.  **Cancellation of Iraq-Saudi PM Meeting:** Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's planned visit to Saudi Arabia was cancelled following the US-Saudi joint airstrikes in Iraq.
8.  **IDF Kills PIJ Commander in Gaza:** The IDF killed Muhammad Khalil Muhammad Aslam, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander, in Khan Younis, who was involved in the abduction of Israeli civilians on October 7, 2023.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high across the Middle East. The direct ballistic missile exchange between Iran and the US (albeit with reported interceptions) and the joint US-Saudi strikes in Iraq represent a significant escalation from previous proxy confrontations, increasing the likelihood of further retaliatory cycles. President Trump's aggressive rhetoric ("beat the fucking shit out of Iran") further exacerbates this risk.

Active flashpoints include Iraq, where the US-Saudi strikes and Iranian-backed militia casualties have prompted strong condemnations from Iraqi leaders, calls for US expulsion, and threats of retaliation against Saudi Arabia. The Strait of Hormuz remains highly volatile, with Iran's explicit intent to control the waterway and threats to European vessels raising the specter of direct naval confrontations. The southern Lebanon buffer zone is another flashpoint, with Hezbollah's drone attack marking the first ceasefire violation and prompting Israeli deliberation on a response.

Military postures are hardening: Iran is reportedly acquiring advanced shoulder-fired air defense systems from China to bolster its defenses. The US and Saudi Arabia are conducting joint offensive operations. The IDF has reopened a naval helicopter squadron, indicating increased maritime readiness, and is preparing responses to Lebanese provocations.

Red lines are actively being tested and crossed. Iran views any foreign military presence in the Strait of Hormuz as a direct challenge to its sovereignty and a legitimate target. Iraqi leadership views the US-Saudi strikes as a "blatant violation" of its sovereignty. Hezbollah's drone attack directly violated the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire agreement.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US posture** is one of strong deterrence and direct engagement. President Trump threatened severe military action against Iran, including striking bridges and power plants, if a new agreement is not reached. He also stated that US/Saudi strikes in Iraq were coordinated with the Iraqi government, a claim contradicted by Iraqi officials. The US Senate advanced a bill to extend sanctions on Iran and impose new ones on Russia. CENTCOM publicly confirmed the interception of Iranian ballistic missiles over Jordan and issued a warning to US troops regarding sensitive information leaks via mobile phones.

**Gulf states** are divided. Saudi Arabia actively participated in joint strikes in Iraq and reported intercepting drones from Iran-backed militias, while its planned meeting with Iraq's PM was cancelled. Oman continues its mediating role for the Strait of Hormuz, proposing transit fee models, though Iran rejected key elements of the proposal.

**EU members** France and Britain reportedly refused a US request to join an international maritime task force in the Strait of Hormuz, citing frustration with the Trump administration's lack of consultation on Iran strikes and a preference for a permanent ceasefire with Iran. The EU's foreign policy chief engaged in discussions with Iran's Foreign Minister on regional developments.

**Russia** stated that Ukraine's attack on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea should be considered an attack on Iran, and its embassy in Iraq offered condolences for casualties from the US-Saudi strikes.

**China** called for de-escalation in the Red Sea and resumption of negotiations in the Persian Gulf. Concurrently, Reuters reported that China is a supplier of shoulder-fired air-defense missiles to Iran.

**Turkey** was mentioned in the context of internal political developments, with no direct statements on the current Iran war or Middle East situation.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions are evident in the reporting: An early report from N12 and Asaf Roz quoting a senior American official claimed "there was no attack" in Iraq, which was later contradicted by official US CENTCOM and Saudi confirmations of joint strikes. There is a clear discrepancy regarding coordination: Trump claimed US-Saudi strikes in Iraq were coordinated with the Iraqi government, which Iraqi leadership explicitly denied, condemning the strikes as a violation of sovereignty. On Iranian missile effectiveness in Jordan, CENTCOM reported all missiles were intercepted with no damage or casualties, while Iran's IRGC, via Press TV, claimed 200+ "enemy forces" were killed. Similarly, Iran's FM reported Ukraine stating its attack on an Iranian ship was unintentional, yet Ukrainian President Zelensky had previously accepted official responsibility for a "conscious attack."

Several unverified claims are present, including the high casualty count of "200+ enemy forces dead" from Iranian missile strikes in Jordan (Press TV), and alarmist reports from Hebrew media of "war has begun, region is exploding." Claims about specific civilian targets in Iraq, such as pilgrim guesthouses in Karbala, appear in biased channels (omid dana, kianmeli1) and lack independent verification. Citizen reports of missile launches from Khomin and lights in the sky over Lorestan are unconfirmed. A claim regarding Melania Trump's absence from Senator Graham's memorial due to Iranian threats is reported by Newsweek but remains unverified.

Propaganda indicators are strong in certain sources, particularly omid dana, which employs highly inflammatory and sectarian language, expressing open support for attacks on Iraqi Shiite targets. Press TV also frequently presents narrative-driven content and offers explicit viewpoints and features aligning with Iranian state messaging, as exemplified by its "Hormuz, the story of a strait" documentaries and the unverified high casualty figures attributed to Iranian strikes.

Reporting gaps include the lack of detailed specifics on the locations and nature of all US-Saudi targets in Iraq beyond broad categories, and the absence of independent confirmation or details regarding the three tankers Iran claimed to have struck in the Strait of Hormuz.
